1) One-way exclusion: Willow is proposing a one-way exclusion of consequential/special/incidental/punitive damages to the extent they arise from use of the Service, but explicitly reserving consequential damages for third-party claims and data loss.
2) Punitive carve-out: we want punitive damages removed from the exclusion (i.e., allow punitive where applicable under law).

Laura / Rishi — forwarding Willow's redline and the two asks (one-way consequential exclusion + carve-out for punitive). They say procurement can't proceed without resolution. Quick background: Willow is a mid-market analytics platform, likely to take Dedicated once committed. Risk: their one-way exclusion would leave us exposed on downstream third-party claims.

Questions for legal:
- Are we comfortable agreeing to a one-way exclusion (customer only seeking to exclude their liability to Redwood)?
- If not, can you propose a mutual formulation that is likely to satisfy their procurement team?
- Do we have flexibility on punitive carve-outs in states where punitive damages are allowed (e.g., where willful misconduct applies)?

I drafted a short compromise (see attached Monica_Proposed_Language.docx) that keeps mutuality but narrows the punitive carve-out to "willful or grossly negligent conduct" and adds a short definition for consequential damages tied to "foreseeable business loss". Can you review and advise whether this is acceptable to present?

Thanks — happy to jump on a 15-min call if easier.

Subject: Re: Fwd: Willow redline — damages & exclusions (MSA v3)

Monica — reviewed. High-level guidance: we should avoid one-way exclusions that would materially reduce Redwood's defenses to third-party claims. Suggested approach: propose a mutual exclusion but accept a limited punitive exception tied strictly to "willful misconduct" and statutory obligations. Key points and suggested language: 

- Mutual carve-out: both parties exclude consequential/special/incidental/punitive damages except as set forth below.
- Punitive/willful: remove punitive only to the extent awarded for a party's willful or intentional misconduct, as determined by a court of competent jurisdiction.
- Definition narrowness: define "Consequential Damages" as "losses of revenue, profits, business interruption, and loss of data that were reasonably foreseeable at the time of contracting."
- Cap preservation: keep overall liability cap tied to the greater of fees paid in the prior 12 months or $1,000,000.

Draft snippet you can send: 
"Except for damages arising from (a) a party's gross negligence or willful misconduct, or (b) a party's breach of confidentiality or data protection obligations, or (c) claims by third parties for bodily injury or death, neither party shall be liable to the other for consequential, incidental, special, exemplary or punitive damages, including loss of profits, loss of business or loss of data, even if such party has been advised of the possibility of such damages. "

This preserves our protections while giving Willow a limited path for punitive relief where their counsel insists. If Willow insists on one-way language, push back: request a contractual premium (credit/discount) and limit the scope (only claims arising out of Willow's use of the Service, exclude third-party downstream claims).

If you want, I can draft an edit and I recommend we copy Prod Security for any data-loss carve-out.

-Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Associate General Counsel | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Willow redline — damages & exclusions (MSA v3)

Sara — thanks for the redline and patience while we reviewed this with legal. After internal review, Redwood can accept a mutual exclusion with a limited punitive/willful-misconduct carve-out and a tightened definition of consequential damages. Key points: 

- Mutuality: the exclusion will apply to both parties (not one-way).
- Punitive carve-out: punitive damages remain excluded except where awarded for a party's willful or intentional misconduct as determined by a court.
- Consequential definition: we've clarified consequential damages to mean reasonably foreseeable losses such as lost revenue, lost profits, business interruption, and loss of data.
- Liability cap: unchanged — the cap will remain the greater of fees paid in the prior 12 months or $1,000,000.

Proposed next steps: 
1) Please confirm whether the mutual formulation above (we'll send exact language in-track once you confirm) would be acceptable to Willow procurement/legal.
2) If yes, we'll prepare an updated redline and DocuSign envelope for execution. DocuSign prep link: https://app.docusign.com/prepare/WIL-2026-0821

If they cannot accept mutual language, we can discuss limited one-way concessions but would need a commercial offset (e.g., a 10% discount on the first-year committed fees or a temporary SLA credit).

Would you like the exact contract snippet now? I can attach the draft proposed language for your counsel to review.

Best,
